title: OSD fingerprint 0.7
description: What a detection observed of one device plugged in, and the device the person confirmed it is. Matched against device descriptors (their identity block and controls) to recognise a model that does not identify itself; confirmed fingerprints teach the next detection; one of a device no descriptor describes yet, with the controls the person named, starts its descriptor. It holds nothing about the person or the machine: port names are kept as their words, without numbers.

^_.description: A note for people; never read by a program.

sources.description: Where the data comes from, with its credit, licence and the firmware it documents.

via.description: A web browser (no USB identity) or a program on the machine.

platform.description: The platform the observation was taken on (in a browser, the host's); unknown when absent.

stack.description: The naming stack, when the tool knows it; it requires its platform.

endpoint_name.description: The name the device gives its own MIDI 2.0 UMP endpoint, as observed, lower case as the port names are.

product_instance_id.description: The MIDI 2.0 product instance id of the unit, as observed; compared exactly. It tells two units of one model apart, so no device descriptor holds it.

^_.description: A note for people; never read by a program.

ports.description: The device's MIDI port names, lower case, words only.

identity_reply.description: Its answer to the Universal Identity Request, hex.

^_.description: A note for people; never read by a program.

maker_replies.description: Read-only maker requests sent (those a device descriptor names) and what came back.

^_.description: A note for people; never read by a program.

controls.description: The controls that arrived while the person turned knobs, in order, without their values.

^_.description: A note for people; never read by a program.

descriptor.description: The OSD device descriptor it is (maker/file).

device.description: The device the fingerprint was taken on, with its firmware: a device of the catalogue (descriptor) or one the person declares (vendor and model, as they name it). A device and a program are exclusive.

^_.description: A note for people; never read by a program.

program.description: A firmware or an application the fingerprint was taken on, in the words of its card (name, version, kind), whatever device it runs on.

names.description: Controls the person named while teaching it: what a control does, in their words or a common address name (filter cutoff).

^_.description: A note for people; never read by a program.
